defect.description: A NETRC path is still expanded under the home directory: os.path.expanduser(f"~/{name}") turns NETRC=/etc/ci/netrc into a path like /home/user//etc/ci/netrc, so a NETRC file outside the home directory (an absolute path, or one starting with ~) is never found and no credentials are returned; only the default NETRC_FILES names should get the ~/ prefix.

review_items: netrc_auth.py:17 unconditionally prepends ~/ to NETRC env value, producing wrong path for absolute NETRC
test uses bare filename for NETRC, masking the line-17 bug; add absolute path test
empty NETRC string treated as valid, causing home directory lookup
votes.evidence_quote: `f"~/{name}"` unconditionally prepends `~/` to the NETRC env var value.
votes.justification: The review's first finding points at the expanduser call in get_netrc_auth and names the same cause: the ~/ prefix is applied to the NETRC value, so an absolute path resolves under home. It also gives the same fix: use the value directly and only expand ~ if present. The exact resolved path differs slightly (/home/user/etc/... rather than /home/user//etc/...), but the faulty behaviour and its cause are the same.
